evidence.note: Diagnosed OutOfResources as too many simultaneous weight loads → redesigned to sequential loading; then diagnosed illegal memory access to a stride-offset bug and fixed it. Specific-cause fixes with re-verification.

Abandoned the slow custom contraction kernel for torch.matmul (perf pivot); tried FP16 for speed, hit NaNs on Cauchy, correctly root-caused FP16 overflow on heavy tails and switched to bfloat16 — cleanly separating a performance change from a numerical-stability failure.

bfloat16 broke the 2e-2 tolerance → reverted contraction to float32/TF32; built debug scripts to isolate the divergence and traced it to a TF32 precision mismatch vs the reference, then aligned precision and added float64 LayerNorm accumulation. Deliberate, oracle-validated design changes.
torch.compile caused precision failures; removed it to preserve correctness despite the latency cost — a principled trade-off refusing to sacrifice the correctness gate for speed.
Precision-tuning phase shows some oscillation (toggling TF32/FP16/BF16/compile across many iterations) before converging, which keeps this below the top anchor.

reasoning: The agent repeatedly diagnosed failures to root cause and made deliberate design changes validated against its reference — distinguishing math/contract issues (stride/offset), numerical-precision issues (FP16 overflow on Cauchy, TF32 mismatch, float64 LN accumulation), and perf problems (abandoning the slow custom kernel), matching the level-8 anchor. It also demonstrated the correctness/latency trade-off by removing torch.compile to protect the correctness gate. It stops short of 10 because the extended precision phase oscillated across TF32/FP16/BF16/compile settings before converging rather than isolating each divergence in a single clean pass.
